title: Old Navy vs. Lands' End: The tall-plus sweatpant problem is really two size systems
summary: A 31–33-inch inseam, curvier waist-to-hip ratio, cotton-rich fleece, pockets, and a plus size should be compatible requirements. Old Navy and Lands' End show why shoppers still have to verify whether tall and plus are offered together.
author: Curvy& Editorial

sections.heading: Tall and plus are separate filters until a product proves otherwise
paragraphs: A recent r/PlusSizeFashion request was unusually precise: at least a 31-inch inseam, preferably 33, a 12-inch difference between hip and waist, at least 50% cotton, pockets, and ideally a price below $50. Community members pointed to Old Navy, but the shopper noted that the brand's sizing had not consistently matched their proportions. That tension is the real brief: length alone does not solve the waistband and hip fit.

Retailers often display Tall and Plus as neighboring ranges even when one garment cannot combine them. Before comparing colors or discounts, confirm that the size selector permits your width and length at the same time.

sections.heading: Old Navy currently combines the two axes on selected sweats
paragraphs: Old Navy's current High-Waisted SoComfy Wide-Leg Sweatpants list a 33.5-inch tall inseam, a drawstring waist, on-seam pockets, and fabric that is 90% cotton and 10% recycled polyester. The product page shows Tall alongside sizes through 4X. That is a rare near-exact match for the community brief, although prices, colors, final-sale status, and size availability vary by selection.

For a narrower leg, the current Extra High-Waisted Logo Sweatpants list a 31.5-inch tall inseam, 80% cotton fleece, pockets, a drawstring, and sizes through 4X. The extra-high rise sits above the belly button and the cuffed leg changes how length behaves: a 31.5-inch jogger can stay anchored at the ankle, while a 33.5-inch wide leg needs enough shoe clearance to avoid dragging.

sections.heading: A 12-inch hip-to-waist difference still needs a fit strategy
paragraphs: Old Navy's current bottoms chart puts 2X across roughly a 42–44.25-inch waist and 51.5–53.75-inch hip, with larger sizes preserving a broadly similar relationship. Someone with a 12-inch difference may need the hip column before the waist column. In a pull-on sweatpant, the drawstring can manage modest waist excess; it cannot add room through a strained seat or upper thigh.

Measure a successful pair flat at the relaxed waist, fully extended waist, fullest hip, front rise, back rise, thigh, and inseam. Brand body charts identify the starting label, but those finished-garment measurements reveal whether a wide-leg or jogger pattern can accommodate your particular curve without relying on an over-tight drawcord.

sections.heading: Lands' End offers the lengths, but not always in the plus range
paragraphs: Lands' End Serious Sweats joggers meet several material requirements: 84% cotton fleece, a drawstring, and a 31-inch Tall inseam. The catch is structural. The page lists Tall in XS–XL, while its separate Plus range has a 28-inch inseam. The brand's Sport Knit pants repeat the split: Tall reaches 32 inches in straight sizes, while Plus is approximately 29.5 inches.

That makes Lands' End a strong option if your body measurements fit its straight-size XL and you need 31–32 inches. It does not satisfy a shopper who needs both a plus width and the tall inseam in these specific styles. A brand can carry Tall and Plus without carrying Tall Plus, and the product-level selector—not the department menu—settles the question.

sections.heading: Which is the better first order?
paragraphs: Try Old Navy first when you need a labeled 2X–4X and at least a 31-inch inseam in the same garment. Choose the SoComfy wide leg for the longest listed inseam and a roomier line; choose the Logo jogger when 31.5 inches is sufficient and a cuff helps control the hem. Try Lands' End first only when its straight-size chart fits your waist and hip, or when the shorter Plus inseam actually matches your preferred break.

Check the exact color and size for return eligibility before paying, especially on clearance. During try-on, sit and climb stairs to test the rise, then walk in the intended shoes to test length. A good tall-plus sweatpant has to clear the hip, stay at the waist without painful cinching, and reach the ankle; satisfying only two of those three is still a fit miss.
bullets: Filter by size first, then verify Tall remains selectable.
Use the hip measurement to protect mobility and the drawstring only for fine adjustment.
Confirm cotton percentage on the exact color because blends can vary within a style.

researchNote: This guide responds to a September 2026 community request and verifies inseams, fiber content, pockets, size availability, and official charts at the product level. Availability and sale terms can change; fit also varies with rise preference, waist-to-hip proportion, and intended shoe.
